set.descent_text: A V-thread at the top is the descent anchor; it holds up well and can be backed up with a second screw or thread before rappelling off.
set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Bozo's Revenge is toward the right-hand end of the bench, past Joy After Pain.

review.notes: Route page: V-thread at top, location right end of bench; area page: parking and trail to bench.

set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Joy After Pain sits on the right side of the bench, with Pillars of the Community to its left and Bozo's Revenge to its right. The line follows a drainage with a steep curtain and pillar at the start and a final steep step high in the drainage.

review.notes: Location relative to neighbours from route page; parking/trail from area page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Climb the route and make a V-thread to rappel back down to the drainage. The base can be mixed if the ice has melted out, so carry sling material for threads.
set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Legal At Last lies in the amphitheater above The Moratorium: climb or hike The Moratorium and keep going up the drainage until the route comes into view on the left side of the amphitheater.

review.notes: Route page gives location above Moratorium and the V-thread descent.

set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Mean Streak is the central flow of the bench when it forms, between The One Hitter and The Moratorium, just left of Natural Immunity.

review.notes: Location only; no descent stated.

set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Pillars of the Community is left of Joy After Pain along the bench; the first pitch is a narrow slot guarded by a chockstone.

review.notes: Location relative to Joy After Pain; no descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route. Build a V-thread at the top of the second pitch if none is in place, and aim for the small shelf on the left at the top of the first pitch for the lower rappel. Leaving the screws from the first belay in place gives you something to clip while setting up. The last rappel is straightforward.
set.approach: Hunter Creek Road has a pull-off from which the route is visible, and a parking area on a two-track nearby also serves the bench. The approach crosses flat ground and then gains a lot of height to reach the base, and is widely regarded as the hardest part of the day. Snow can slow the climb up.

review.notes: Two sources agree rappel route by V-thread; approach described as long in both. Counts omitted.

set.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. The One Hitter is at the left end of the bench, well left of The Moratorium.

review.notes: Location only; no descent stated.

set.approach: Driving into the South Fork valley, Welcome Wagon is the first obvious flow up to the right, forming on volcanic cliffs just above the road. Park off the road and walk the short way up to the base.

review.notes: Two pages agree on the location and short approach. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route from trees; bring webbing for slinging them. The same trees and V-thread anchors used on The Schoolhouse Route serve the lower part of the descent.
set.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Cross the sage prairie toward the drainage just left of the prominent Schoolhouse Spire and follow the drainage to the first pitches of The Schoolhouse Route. Classroom Bully carries on from the top of that route's third pitch, taking the left branch of the drainage.

review.notes: Route pages give extension of Schoolhouse Route and tree rappels; parking from Schoolhouse page.

set.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road, and take the Illogicicle drainage, the second drainage east of Schoolhouse Creek. The route is in the main amphitheater just right of the first pitch of Illogicicle; it is often climbed as a way around that pitch when it has not formed.

review.notes: Location in amphitheater and parking from the two route pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Cross the sagebrush, bear left around a small hill, and go up the main drainage toward its left fork, scrambling in places; the Illogicicle amphitheater is the second drainage east of Schoolhouse Creek. Snow slows the approach.

review.notes: Approach from the route page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The first pitch comes down from a V-thread and the pitches above use trees; bring webbing to sling them.
set.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Using the three-spired Schoolhouse Spire as a landmark, hike across the sage prairie to the drainage just left of it, then follow the drainage up to a fork and take the right-hand branch. The drainage is steep in places and needs care around chockstones and boulders.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach, V-thread on pitch one and trees above.

set.approach: Start at the Boulder Basin trailhead on Hunter Creek Road and follow the Boulder Basin trail to its first switchback, where it turns back on itself nearly 180 degrees. From there, head up and left and follow the drainage to the base of the curtain.

review.notes: Approach from route page; the anchor tree is a snag, not a descent. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start at the Boulder Basin trailhead on Hunter Creek Road and follow the Boulder Basin trail to its second switchback. Head up and right, staying out of the drainage, to reach the base of the pillar. A higher line to the left above short cliff bands is exposed to avalanche terrain, so stay out of it unless conditions are known. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Approach and avalanche note from route page; neighbouring page says Hunter Creek Falls is rappelled.

set.approach: Start at the Boulder Basin trailhead on Hunter Creek Road, or walk up from the Lower Bench parking area, and follow the trail uphill to the Upper Bench. It is a steady, sustained climb to the base of the flow.

review.notes: Approach from route and area pages. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel the upper pitches. Below the second pitch, traverse across to Hunter Creek Falls and rappel that, then walk back down the approach and talus to the trailhead.
set.approach: Park at the Boulder Basin trailhead on Hunter Creek Road and go through the fence at the lot; the trail heads southeast right away. Stay on the established horse trail; the old two-track beside it does not save time. Then leave gates as you found them. At the second switchback leave the trail to the west, traverse at about the same height into a talus field, and climb through it to enter the Hunter Creek Falls drainage.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach and the descent; counts left out.

set.descent_text: Walk off by the trail on the right of the climb, as you look at it.
set.approach: Park at the Boulder Basin trailhead and head for the Flying H Ranch gully immediately southwest of Ice Fest. Work up the drainage into a chute of moderate angle, then cross over from its left side to reach the ice.

review.notes: Route page gives location, approach and walk-off.

set.descent_text: If the cleft holds ice, build a V-thread to descend. Without ice the anchor is not established, so be prepared to make your own.
set.approach: Park at the Boulder Basin trailhead and head up to the Flying H Ranch cliffs. The route is the cleft in the first gully right of Horse Tail Falls.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Make a zero-thread anchor and rappel the route with two long ropes.
set.approach: From the Boulder Basin trailhead the trail leads up and right past a gate, which should be left as found, and on around another bend or two. Leave the trail rightward, crossing a gully or two depending on your line, to gain the right side of the drainage, then pick through fallen timber and climb the drainage to the ice.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Walk off through the gully immediately left of the route.
set.approach: Park at the Boulder Basin trailhead and head toward the Flying H Ranch cliffs. Stay on the ridge left of the drainage until you are close to the route, which has a large cave in the rock beside the ice most of the way up.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Park at the Boulder Basin trailhead and take the trail toward the far end of Flying H Ranch, which leads to Sheepeater Creek, a wide open drainage. Hike up the creek over small ice steps to the main first pitch. After the second pitch, coil the ropes and walk the creek bed to a major junction, where the third pitch is visible up and to the right.

review.notes: Route page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel from a V-thread at the top of the first pitch. From the top of the final curtain, rappel from a tree to the left of the curtain's top; the tree can be hard to reach and rocks can be knocked down while pulling the ropes. Bring webbing and two ropes.
set.approach: Park past the Ishawooa Mesa trail, then hike across the sage prairie toward the obvious drainage; the upper pitches are visible from the road. As you enter the drainage, walk uphill to its left to reach the base of the route.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Slow Turning continues above Stringer: climb Stringer to near the top of its second pitch, where a small drip on the right leads up to the line. Reaching the last two hard pitches takes a long hike.

review.notes: Route page. No descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel from a V-thread on the last pitch using two ropes, or walk off to the right.
set.approach: Park off the road in the small pullouts a short way past the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead, just below the Legg Creek drainage on the north side of the valley. The climb is in the Slow Turning drainage canyon. The walk is short and casual, with a couple of small steps of ice bouldering right before the first pitch.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Park along the road on the north side of the valley, cross the valley floor, and follow Legg Creek up to the first pitch.

review.notes: Route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Legg Creek's opening pitch gets you into the upper basin; then follow the main drainage up over snow; the first pitch of Ovisight is obvious on the left as a skinny pillar or hanging fang. From the top of the second pitch, hike up and left a short way to the base of the third.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Climb the first pitch of Legg Creek to reach the upper drainage, then either angle left up the gully beneath the route, or contour across the hillside under the cliff band from the base of Ovisight's first pitch.

review.notes: Route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the end of the South Fork Road, head upriver past Majo Ranch, and cross the river; the crossing changes through the season. Climb a steep hillside trending left toward a rock wall, follow steep game trails to the talus at a rock band, then follow the band around to the base. The route is just left of the Mean Green drainage.

review.notes: Route page and area page. Descent only a guess on the page, so none written.

set.descent_text: Rappel the steeper ice and downclimb the lower-angle steps and rock down the drainage. Bolts sit at the base of the second and third pitches, and a tree is at the top of the third.
set.approach: Park at the end of the South Fork Road, head upriver past Majo Ranch, and cross the South Fork Shoshone River. Walk straight toward the ice, get into the gully early, and follow it to the base. High on Boulder is the wide flow just right of Mean Green.

review.notes: Route page and neighbour page and report agree on rappel plus downclimbing the drainage.

set.descent_text: Rappel V-threads and downclimb the small ice steps between them. Carry a headlamp, since the descent can run late.
set.approach: Park at the end of the road and follow the trail around the fenced ranch. After crossing the river, a riverbank trail leads back down to the Mean Green drainage, which you then ascend on foot; the approach is short. The upper slopes can be wind-loaded and are avalanche terrain. Check the avalanche forecast before heading in.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route, building V-threads from the ice.
set.approach: Park at the end of the road, cross the river to the riverside trail, and follow it to the base of the flow, which is the one right of High on Boulder in the same drainage.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Rappel from the slung tree at the top.
set.approach: Climb High on Boulder first, then continue up its drainage past short ice steps. The route is not visible until you are fairly close; leave the drainage to the right and traverse to the base.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: Start up High on Boulder and belay from screws at the top of its second pitch; the route is a harder alternative to that route's third pitch, off to the left.

review.notes: Route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Hike upstream along the South Fork Shoshone River and cross it, then follow the High on Boulder drainage. Work back left into the drainage higher than High on Boulder, follow it as far as Pillar of Pain, then walk around the ridge to the next small drainage east.

review.notes: Route page. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Begin on the lower pitches of Mean Green. The second pitch starts level with Mean Green's fourth and to the right of it; from the end of the third pitch, traverse left to the bottom of Mean Green's fifth.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Rappel the pillar, then continue down the drainage, rappelling High on Boulder on the way. Gear left at the junction of High on Boulder and Moonrise can be collected on the way out.
set.approach: Climb or walk up the drainage past Moonrise and High on Boulder, then go up a steppy drainage to a rubble slope that leads into the next drainage on the left. The pillar sits a short way east of there. It is steep and sustained, so the approach is demanding.

review.notes: Route page and report agree on rappels down the drainage.
